title: A 2-Inch Shrimp Flips a Starfish Over and Eats It Alive for Days

scenes.text: This two-inch shrimp eats only one thing: living starfish.
Harlequin shrimp live in pairs on coral reefs and look like painted porcelain. Their prey is often bigger than they are.
Working together, the pair flips a starfish onto its back. Upside down, it can't get away.
Then they start eating, softest parts first, beginning with the feet. The starfish stays alive the whole time.
A single four-inch starfish keeps a pair fed for about a week.
Sometimes the starfish tears off its own arm and crawls away. The shrimp keep the arm.

description:
The harlequin shrimp, about two inches long, feeds only on starfish. A bonded pair flips one onto its back to immobilise it, then eats it alive over a period of days, starting with the soft tube feet.
A four-inch sea star can keep a pair occupied for about a week, and the shrimp even take on the coral-eating crown-of-thorns. Sometimes the star escapes by leaving an arm behind.
Beautiful or horrifying: which is it?
subject: harlequin shrimp
first_comment: Harlequin shrimp also eat the crown-of-thorns starfish, the one that devours coral reefs. Hero or villain?
